records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out of the request, and if filtering leaves zero guests the error surfaced is the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. A user who submits one blacklisted address among three sees 'Guests added' success and never learns one email was dropped; a user whose entire submission was filtered is told their emails were invalid/duplicate, sending them debugging the wrong problem.
records.rationale: Verified in addGuests.handler.ts: uniqueGuests filters out emails matching existing attendees or BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with no feedback; if uniqueGuests.length === 0 it throws the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error, and partial filtering results in silent success with dropped emails. This is real, diff-introduced incorrect behavior.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Email delivery failures are swallowed with `catch (err) { console.log(...) }` and the handler still returns success. If all notification emails fail (SMTP outage, template error), the UI shows the success toast 'Guests added', the organizer believes guests were notified, and the only trace is a bare console.log with no error detail and no retry path.
records.rationale: The diff verifiably shows `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` followed by an unconditional `return { message: "Guests added" }` in addGuests.handler.ts, so a total email delivery failure is swallowed and the UI toast 'guests_added' still fires. The described mechanism (silent failure, success feedback, no error detail/retry) is accurate to the code shown. Whether maintainer's consider this an accepted pattern (emails non-critical) is debatable, so confidence is moderate.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Guest deduplication is a check-then-insert on an in-memory read of attendees followed by createMany, with no unique constraint cited on (bookingId, email) to back it. Two concurrent addGuests calls (e.g. a double-click before isPending disables the button, or two tabs) both read the same attendee list, both pass the filter, and both insert the same guest, yielding duplicate Attendee rows for one booking; the app-level filter cannot enforce the invariant that a booking's attendee emails are unique.
records.rationale: The diff shows addGuests.handler.ts reads booking.attendees via findFirst, filters uniqueGuests in memory, then createMany without any unique constraint enforcement shown in the diff. Two concurrent mutations would both pass the filter and insert duplicate attendees. The mechanism (check-then-insert race) is directly verifiable in the diff; the frontend loading state (isPending) mitigates but does not prevent double submission (double-fire before re-render, or two tabs).

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length, and any authenticated attendee of a booking passes the permission check, so a single request can create an arbitrarily large attendee list. Any logged-in user who is an attendee on one booking can submit thousands of email addresses in one mutation, causing mass attendee-row creation, a large updateCalendarAttendees payload, and spam-volume emails sent from the organizer's and app's address to arbitrary recipients.
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: addGuests.schema.ts defines guests: z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length, and addGuests.handler.ts permits any booking attendee (isAttendee check) to call it, creating attendee rows for the full unbounded array, calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails to all supplied addresses. This is a real abuse vector introduced by this change.

A user who pastes a list where some emails are already attendees sees 'Guests added' and has no way to know part of their input was discarded; if they later re-submit the dropped ones expecting clarity, they hit the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error instead of an explanation.
records.rationale: The diff shows uniqueGuests filters out already-attendee and blacklisted emails; if any survive, the handler creates only those and returns { message: "Guests added" } with no indication of skipped emails. If none survive it throws the generic 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This is verifiable in the diff and constitutes silently discarding user input without feedback — a real behavioral defect in the new endpoint.

A user who once submitted invalid input, then closes via success or the X/overlay, reopens the dialog for another booking and sees a validation error banner before typing anything — misdirecting them into thinking their fresh input is invalid.

So a stale validation banner can persist into the next dialog session, as described. It's a minor UX defect but a real, verifiable incorrect behavior introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The authorization gate is computed but its team branch can never authorize non-owner admins because it requires isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner, collapsing the intended admin-or-owner check to owner-only; meanwhile the attendee branch grants full add-guests power on email equality alone. Fail-closed for team admins (denied despite intended access — correctness), but the effective security envelope is asymmetric: any booking attendee passes authorization with zero role verification (a bare email string match against user.email), which is the trust-the-client-adjacent surface that any future expansion of this handler (more mutations, more data returned) will silently inherit.

records.issue_text: [BUG] updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with an EventManager built from ctx.user (the acting user) and their credentials, but the permission branch deliberately permits non-organizer actors (attendees) to trigger this path. When an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar attendee update runs against the attendee's calendar credentials instead of the booking owner's, so the organizer's calendar event attendee list is never updated while the DB and emails say the guests were added — the non-organizer path the permission model opened was never reconciled with the calendar-write path that assumes the organizer is acting.

records.issue_text: [BUG] When a non-organizer (team member or attendee) adds guests, EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` — the caller's credentials — and `updateCalendarAttendees` is then run against the organizer's booking. For any caller other than the booking owner, the calendar attendee update executes with the wrong user's calendar credentials; the organizer's calendar event is not found/updated (or the call errors), leaving the DB attendee list and the real calendar event permanently out of sync.
records.rationale: The diff explicitly builds the EventManager from the caller: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and then `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`.
